skill.name: operating-production-services
skill.description: SRE patterns for production reliability, including SLOs, error budgets, postmortems, incident response, and alerting guidance.
skill.summary: Apply SRE patterns for SLOs, error budgets, incidents, and postmortems.

content.value_statement: Production services need clear reliability targets and repeatable incident practices. This skill guides SLOs, error budgets, alerting, and postmortems.
actual_capabilities: Explains the relationship between SLAs, SLOs, and SLIs.
Provides PromQL examples for availability and latency SLIs.
Maps error budget levels to release and reliability actions.
Supplies standard and quick postmortem templates.
References burn-rate alerting patterns for Prometheus and Grafana.
Gives facilitation guidance for blameless postmortem meetings.
limitations: Does not deploy monitoring rules or modify production systems.
Requires teams to adapt example PromQL to their metrics names.
Does not replace incident commander judgment during active incidents.
Does not cover initial service scaffolding or application design.

use_cases.title: Define Service SLOs
use_cases.description: Create practical availability and latency targets with matching SLIs and error budget policies.

use_cases.title: Improve Incident Reviews
use_cases.description: Use blameless postmortem templates to document impact, timeline, root cause, and action items.

use_cases.title: Design Burn-Rate Alerts
use_cases.description: Plan Prometheus alerts that combine short and long windows to reduce noise and catch fast failures.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an SLO Target
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new production service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose availability and latency SLOs for a customer-facing API. Include error budget impact and tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Postmortem
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a blameless postmortem for this incident summary. Include timeline, impact, root cause, and action items.

prompt_templates.title: Review Alert Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced monitoring review for an existing service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our current SLO alerting approach and suggest multi-window burn-rate alerts for availability and latency.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Reliability Operating Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an operating model for SLO governance, error budget decisions, incident reviews, and recurring reliability improvements.

output_examples.input: We need a 99.9 percent availability SLO for an API.
output_examples.output: A practical response explains the monthly error budget, defines good and total request measurements, and suggests release actions when budget falls.

output_examples.input: We had a 40 minute checkout outage yesterday.
output_examples.output: A useful output includes an executive summary, timeline, impact section, 5 Whys analysis, and assigned follow-up actions.

output_examples.input: Our alerts are noisy during small latency spikes.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests burn-rate alerts with short and long windows, plus dashboard fields that show current budget and trend.

best_practices: Start with user-visible SLIs before choosing alert thresholds.
Attach every postmortem action item to an owner, date, and tracking ticket.
Use error budgets to guide release risk instead of treating SLOs as absolute promises.
anti_patterns: Setting 100 percent SLO targets without accepting cost and tradeoffs.
Writing postmortems that blame individuals instead of improving systems.
Alerting on raw symptoms without burn-rate context or user impact.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps teams define SLOs, manage error budgets, write postmortems, and plan SLO-based alerts.

faq.question: Does it operate production systems directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and templates. It does not deploy, restart, or change services.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it include Prometheus examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes PromQL examples and references multi-window burn-rate alert patterns.

faq.question: Is this useful during an active incident?
faq.answer: It can structure thinking, but incident commanders should follow their approved response process.

faq.question: Does it replace a full SRE program?
faq.answer: No. It supplies reusable patterns that teams should adapt to their service and organization.
